h1: Welding positioners — tilting, rotary and lift, 22 to 44,092 lb
intro: A welding positioner holds the part on a turntable and turns it under the torch at a steady, adjustable speed, so a round weld on a flange, pipe-to-plate joint, hub, tank head or wheel is laid in one continuous pass in the flat position — no stopping, repositioning and restarting around the part, and a more even bead whether the torch is held by hand or clamped in a holder. Tilting the table brings the joint to the best angle for the torch. NovoTech has positioners for every size of part, all on this page, small to large: light and benchtop positioners from 22 to 247 lb, with chucks, hollow bores and foot pedals; the premium-line WP 100 and WP 300 tilting positioners, built in Turkey, 220 and 661 lb on single-phase power; value-line tilting positioners from 485 to 2,646 lb; HBT rotary welding tables and HBJ lift positioners that also adjust in height, to 44,092 lb; heavy tilting positioners from 3,307 to 44,092 lb with motorized tilt; headstock and tailstock, L-type and hydraulic positioners built to order; and the chucks and torch holders that go on them. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What does a welding positioner do?
faq.a: It turns the part under a stationary torch at a set speed, so a circumferential weld is made in one pass in the flat position — the easiest position to weld and the one that gives the most even bead. The welder no longer walks around the part or stops to reposition it; with the torch in a holder the travel speed is as steady as the table, which makes repeat parts faster and more uniform.

faq.q: How do I size a positioner for my part?
faq.a: By the weight and where its centre of gravity sits. The rating is for the centre of gravity close to the table centre and face: the further it is from the axis (an off-centre bracket) or from the table (a tall part), the more torque the drive and the tilt need. The tables give the limits — the HB positioners up to 3.9 – 9.8″ off the axis and 5.9 – 23.6″ above the table, the heavy WP positioners 12″ and 12″. For off-centre or tall parts choose the next size up, and send us a sketch with the weight.

faq.q: How fast should the table turn?
faq.a: Table speed (rpm) = travel speed ÷ (π × weld diameter). A MIG weld at 20 in/min around a Ø6″ flange needs about 1.1 rpm; a submerged-arc weld at 20 in/min on a Ø60″ tank head about 0.1 rpm. Check that the positioner's speed range covers your smallest and largest weld diameters: the light positioners turn up to 8 – 18 rpm, the heavy ones as slowly as 0.03 rpm.

faq.q: Tilting positioner, rotary table, lift or headstock positioner?
faq.a: A tilting positioner turns and tilts the part on a table — the most versatile. A rotary welding table (HBT) only turns, for parts that stand upright: tanks, drums, rings and hubs. A lift positioner (HBJ) also adjusts the table height, so the work comes to the welder or the welding head. Headstock and tailstock positioners turn long parts — beams, columns, frames and shafts — about their own length.

faq.q: What can be mounted on the turntable?
faq.a: The tables are T-slotted for clamps, angle plates and fixtures. A self-centring 3-jaw welding chuck holds pipe, shafts and round parts on centre — the WPC chucks on this page grip from Ø0.4″ inside to Ø15″ outside — and a torch holder on an adjustable arm keeps the torch in one place while the part turns.

The WP 100 and WP 300 tilting positioners are built in Turkey for NovoTech's premium line and run on single-phase 220 V with a foot pedal. The other positioners, the turning rolls, the column and boom manipulators, the pipe stands and the tables are NovoTech's value line, built in China to NovoTech's specification — with the same CSA-approved panel, 1-year warranty and parts and support in Canada.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
